messages.subject: GP with repeated x
parts:
Hi folks,

I've been trying to extend the manual's example for fitting a Gaussian Process to the scenario where you have repeated observations at each point on the x-axis. The first approach is to leave the code (https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/blob/master/misc/gaussian-process/gp-fit.stan) as is and simply provide x data with the repeated values. This however unnecessarily increases the size of the matrix Sigma, catastrophically in cases with many repetitions per x-value (i.e. very slow sampling on my low-memory notebook). So I coded the alternative below, which seems to get a great speedup without sacrificing effective sample size. 

However, I'm also looking to get posterior predictions, and I'm uncertain how to apply the examples from the manual amidst data of this structure. Specifically, all the examples where one is generating samples from the posterior involve the data y, and I'm not sure how to handle the fact that y is a matrix (i.e. multiple y values per unique x value). Any suggestions?

Mike


#File: gp-fit2.stan
  data {
    int<lower=1> NX; #num unique X values
    vector[NX] X; #X values
    int<lower=1> NZ; #num repetitions per X
    matrix[NZ,NX] Y; #Y values
  }
  transformed data {
    #convert data Y from matrix to array of row 
    #  vectors (manual says latter is faster)
    row_vector[NX] Y_rv[NZ]; 
    vector[NX] mu; #to be set to zero
    for (nx in 1:NX){
      mu[nx] <- 0;
    }
    for(nz in 1:NZ){
      Y_rv[nz] <- Y[nz];
    }
  }
  parameters {
    real<lower=0> eta_sq;
    real<lower=0> inv_rho_sq;
    real<lower=0> sigma_sq;
  }
  model {
    matrix[NX,NX] Sigma;
    # Sigma off-diagonal
    for (i in 1:(NX-1)) {
      for (j in (i+1):NX) {
        Sigma[i,j] <- eta_sq * exp(- pow(X[i] - X[j],2)/inv_rho_sq);
        Sigma[j,i] <- Sigma[i,j];
      }
    }
    # Sigma diagonal 
    for (k in 1:NX){
      Sigma[k,k] <- eta_sq + sigma_sq; # + jitter 
    }
    #priors on kernel parameters
    eta_sq ~ cauchy(0,5);
    inv_rho_sq ~ cauchy(0,5);
    sigma_sq ~ cauchy(0,5);
    #assert sampling on each row of Y data
    for(nz in 1:NZ){
      Y_rv[nz] ~ multi_normal(mu,Sigma);
    }
  }
# end of file "gp-fit2.stan"

And here's some R code for demo'ing the performance of the standard gp-fit.stan vs gp-fit2.stan amidst x repetitions:

  library(rstan)
  library(ggplot2)

  #load data
  source('gp-fit.data.R')

  #plot the data
  dat = data.frame(x,y)
  ggplot(
    data = dat
    , mapping = aes(
      x = x
      , y = y
    )
  )+
  geom_point()

  #load the standard model
  gp_model = stan_model(file="gp-fit.stan")

  #sample the standard model (no reps in data)
  gp_fit <- sampling(
    gp_model
    , data=list(x=x,N=N,y=y)
    , iter = 2000 #samples very quickly
    , chains = 1
    , cores = 1
    , seed = 1
  )
  print(gp_fit)

  #add x-repetition to the data
  set.seed(1)
  obs_per_x = 10
  #repeat x
  x2 = rep(x,times=obs_per_x)
  #repeat and add some noise to y
  y2 = rep(y,times=obs_per_x)+rnorm(N*obs_per_x,0,sd(y)/4)

  #plot the data
  dat = data.frame(x2,y2,set=rep(c('1','2'),each=length(x),times=obs_per_x))
  ggplot(
    data = dat
    , mapping = aes(
      x = x2
      , y = y2
      , colour = set
    )
  )+
  geom_point()

  #compile the attempted improved model 
  gp_model2 = stan_model(file="gp-fit2.stan")

  #sample the attempted improved model
  gp_fit_with_reps2 <- sampling(
    gp_model2
    , data = list(
      NX = length(x)
      , X = x
      , NZ = obs_per_x
      , Y = matrix(y2, ncol=length(x), byrow=T)
    )
    , iter = 200 #
    , chains = 1
    , cores = 1
    , seed = 1
  )
  print(gp_fit_with_reps2)
  
  #for comparison, sample with the original model
  gp_fit_with_reps <- sampling(
    gp_model
    , data=list(
        x = x2
      , N = length(x2)
      , y = y2
    )
    , iter = 200
    , chains = 1
    , cores = 1
    , seed = 1
  )
  print(gp_fit_with_reps)

parts:
Figured it out! 

Well, somewhat. I can get predictions now, but I came up with different approaches and I'm not quite certain on the inferential meaning of each :Op 

Below is the stan code followed by R-based demonstrations (set your working dir to https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/blob/master/misc/gaussian-process). Could any of you GP-savvy folks take a look and let me know what interpretation you'd put on the different prediction intervals the demo generates?

#file: gp-fit2.stan
  data {
    #NX: num unique X values
    int<lower=1> NX ; 
    #X: x values
    vector[NX] X ; 
    #NZ: num repetitions per X
    int<lower=1> NZ ;
    #Y: matrix of y values
    matrix[NZ,NX] Y ;
    # y_means: across-repetitions by-x means for Y
    vector[NX] Y_means ; 
  }
  transformed data {
    #Y_transpose: for later prediction generation
    matrix[NX,NZ] Y_transpose ;
    #Y_rv: manual says row vectors are faster to loop over
    row_vector[NX] Y_rv[NZ] ; 
    #mu: to be set to zero
    vector[NX] mu ; 
    Y_transpose <- Y' ;

for(nz in 1:NZ){
      Y_rv[nz] <- Y[nz] ;
    }
    for (nx in 1:NX){
      mu[nx] <- 0 ;
    }
  }

parameters {
    #eta_sq: scale of output (Y)
    real<lower=0> eta_sq ;
    #inv_rho_sq: x-axis scale of influence between points (wiggliness?)
    real<lower=0> inv_rho_sq ;
    #sigma_sq: noise scale
    real<lower=0> sigma_sq ;
  }
  transformed parameters{
    #Sigma: covariance matrix

matrix[NX,NX] Sigma ;
    # Sigma off-diagonal
    for (i in 1:(NX-1)) {
      for (j in (i+1):NX) {
        Sigma[i,j] <- eta_sq * exp(- pow(X[i] - X[j],2)/inv_rho_sq) ;
Sigma[j,i] <- Sigma[i,j] ; #lower mirrors upper

}
    }
    # Sigma diagonal 
    for (k in 1:NX){

Sigma[k,k] <- eta_sq + sigma_sq ; # add jitter
    }  
  }
  model {
    #priors on kernel parameters
    eta_sq ~ cauchy(0,1) ;
    inv_rho_sq ~ cauchy(0,1) ;
    sigma_sq ~ cauchy(0,1) ;

#assert sampling on each row of Y data
    for(nz in 1:NZ){
      Y_rv[nz] ~ multi_normal(mu,Sigma) ;
    }
  }

generated quantities {
    #y_preds1: predictions using the Y means
    vector[NX] y_preds1 ;
    #y_preds2: predictionss using each Y
    matrix[NX,NZ] y_preds2 ; 
    { #create sub-enrironment because we don't want to bother saving K
      matrix[NX,NX] K ;
      matrix[NX,NX] K_transpose_div_Sigma ;

      # K all elements
      for (i in 1:NX)
        for (j in 1:NX)
          K[i,j] <- eta_sq * exp(-pow(X[i] - X[j], 2)/inv_rho_sq) ;
   
      K_transpose_div_Sigma <- K' / Sigma ;
      y_preds1 <- K_transpose_div_Sigma * Y_means ;
      y_preds2 <- K_transpose_div_Sigma * Y_transpose ;

    }

  }

#R demo

library(rstan)
  library(ggplot2)

  #load data
  source('gp-fit.data.R')

#rescale x & y for easy prior specification
  x=scale(x)[,1]
  y=scale(y)[,1]

#plot the data
  dat = data.frame(x,y)
  ggplot(
    data = dat
    , mapping = aes(
      x = x
      , y = y
    )
  )+
  geom_point()

  #load the standard model
  gp_model = stan_model(file="gp-fit.stan")

  #sample the standard model (no reps in data)
  gp_fit <- sampling(
    gp_model
    , data=list(x=x,N=N,y=y)
    , iter = 2000 #samples very quickly
    , chains = 1
    , cores = 1
    , seed = 1
  )
alarm()

print(gp_fit)


  #add x-repetition to the data
  set.seed(1)

reps_per_x = 2
  #repeat x
  x2 = rep(x,times=reps_per_x)
#repeat and add some noise to y

y2 = scale(rep(y,times=reps_per_x)+rnorm(N*reps_per_x,0,1))[,1]

  #plot the data
  dat = data.frame(x2,y2,rep_num=factor(rep(1:reps_per_x,each=N)))

ggplot(
    data = dat
    , mapping = aes(
      x = x2
      , y = y2

, group = rep_num
      , colour = rep_num
    )
    , alpha = .5
  )+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()

#compile the attempted improved model 
  gp_model2 = stan_model(file="gp-fit2.stan")

  #sample the attempted improved model
gp_fit_with_reps <- sampling(

gp_model2
    , data = list(
      NX = length(x)
      , X = x
, NZ = reps_per_x
, Y = matrix(y2, ncol=length(x), byrow=T)

, Y_means = colMeans(matrix(y2, ncol=length(x), byrow=T))
    )
    , iter = 2000

, chains = 1
    , cores = 1
    , seed = 1

, pars = 'Sigma' #don't bother including Sigma in saved samples
    , include = FALSE #
  )
  alarm()
  print(gp_fit_with_reps)


  #look at the mean function
  y_preds1 = extract(
    gp_fit_with_reps
    , pars = 'y_preds1'
  )[[1]]
  loci = apply(y_preds1,2,quantile,prob=.025)
  hici = apply(y_preds1,2,quantile,prob=.975)
  p = ggplot()
  p = p + geom_point(

data = dat
    , mapping = aes(
      x = x2
      , y = y2

, colour = rep_num
    )
    , alpha = .5
  )
  p = p + geom_ribbon(
    data = data.frame(
      x = x
      , ymin = loci
      , ymax = hici
    )

, mapping = aes(
      x = x

, ymin = ymin
      , ymax = ymax
    )
    , alpha = .5
  )
  print(p)

  #get predictions for each set
  y_preds2 = extract(
    gp_fit_with_reps
    , pars = 'y_preds2'
  )[[1]]

  #average by x across repetition
  y_preds2a = apply(y_preds2,c(1,2),mean)
  loci = apply(y_preds2a,2,quantile,prob=.025)
  hici = apply(y_preds2a,2,quantile,prob=.975)
  p = ggplot()
  p = p + geom_point(

data = dat
    , mapping = aes(
      x = x2
      , y = y2

, colour = rep_num
    )
    , alpha = .5
  )
  p = p + geom_ribbon(
    data = data.frame(
      x = x
      , ymin = loci
      , ymax = hici
    )

, mapping = aes(
      x = x

, ymin = ymin
      , ymax = ymax
    )
    , alpha = .5
  )
  print(p) #seemingly identical to y_preds1


  #plot each repetition's CI
  p = ggplot()
  p = p + geom_point(

data = dat
    , mapping = aes(
      x = x2
      , y = y2

, colour = rep_num
    )
    , alpha = .5
  )
  for(i in 1:dim(y_preds2)[3]){
    loci = apply(y_preds2[,,i],2,quantile,prob=.025)
    hici = apply(y_preds2[,,i],2,quantile,prob=.975)
    p = p + geom_ribbon(
      data = data.frame(
        x = x
        , ymin = loci
        , ymax = hici
      )

, mapping = aes(
        x = x

, ymin = ymin
        , ymax = ymax
      )
      , alpha = .5
    )
  }
  print(p)

  #gather all replicates and treat as iterations
  y_preds2b = aperm(y_preds2,c(1,3,2))
  dim(y_preds2b) = c(dim(y_preds2)[1]*dim(y_preds2)[3],dim(y_preds2)[2])
  loci = apply(y_preds2b,2,quantile,prob=.025)
  hici = apply(y_preds2b,2,quantile,prob=.975)
  p = ggplot()
  p = p + geom_point(

data = dat
    , mapping = aes(
      x = x2
      , y = y2

, colour = rep_num
    )
    , alpha = .5
  )
  p = p + geom_ribbon(
    data = data.frame(
      x = x
      , ymin = loci
      , ymax = hici
    )

, mapping = aes(
      x = x

, ymin = ymin
      , ymax = ymax
    )
    , alpha = .5
  )
  print(p)



  #for comparison, sample with the original model (takes a lot longer!)
  gp_fit_with_reps2 <- sampling(

gp_model
    , data=list(
        x = x2
      , N = length(x2)
      , y = y2
    )
, iter = 2000

, chains = 1
    , cores = 1
    , seed = 1
  )

alarm()
  print(gp_fit_with_reps2)
